title: Open module cohomology agrees with cohomology of the restricted abelian sheaf
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $\mathcal F$ a sheaf of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $U\subseteq X$ any open, and $p\in\mathbb N$. Let $j:U\to X$ be the induced open subscheme inclusion. There is an additive equivalence between $R^p\Gamma(U,-)(\mathcal F)$ computed in $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] and $H^p(U,(j^*\mathcal F)_{ab})$ computed in abelian sheaves [def-sc-topological-abelian-cohomology]. No quasi-coherence or affineness hypothesis is imposed, and degree zero is included.

source.place: Cohomology, Tag 01E1 (2) (lemma-restrict-injective); Cohomology on Sites, Tag 03FD (lemma-cohomology-modules-abelian-agree)

proof.text: Choose an injective module resolution of F. Restrict it to U using [lem-sc-ringed-space-restrict-injective-resolution]. The equivalence Scheme.Modules.overEquiv U and its overFunctorEquiv identify this resolution with an injective resolution of the restriction along the open immersion U → X. Equivalences preserve injectivity and exactness.

Sections on U of each original term equal global sections on the induced open subscheme of the restricted term. Naturality makes this an isomorphism of section complexes. By [def-sc-open-module-cohomology] and the resolution computation in [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], taking degree-p homology identifies open module cohomology with the underlying additive group of module cohomology of the restricted module. This includes p=0. Use Mathlib InjectiveResolution.isoRightDerivedObj for the additive section functor. The exact forgetful functor from modules over the global ring to additive groups preserves kernels, cokernels and hence homology.

Apply [lem-sc-module-abelian-zariski-cohomology] on the induced scheme U to the restricted module. This identifies module-derived cohomology with the underlying abelian-sheaf cohomology in every degree. The free abelian representable at the terminal open and the constant integer sheaf represent the same functor F ↦ F(U), by the free-forgetful and constant-sheaf adjunctions, so are canonically isomorphic. Precomposition with this isomorphism identifies their Ext groups, hence Sheaf.H′ at top with Sheaf.H, which is Scheme.Modules.H by definition. Compose with Step 2.
